overview: Geely Automobile Holdings is a Hong Kong-listed, Cayman-incorporated Chinese automaker that designs, manufactures and sells passenger vehicles through a multi-brand portfolio spanning mass-market ICE/NEV (Geely, Geely Galaxy), mid-to-high-end (LYNK & CO) and premium NEV (ZEEKR) segments. Following the 2025 privatisation of ZEEKR (delisted from the NYSE) and ZEEKR's acquisition of LYNK & CO from Geely Holding and Volvo Car Corporation, all three core brands are now wholly or majority consolidated under the listco as part of the "One Geely" integration strategy. The Group sells predominantly in China (c.86% of 2025 wholesale volume) with a fast-growing export business (Europe, Latin America, Middle East, Southeast Asia, Australia) and equity stakes in overseas associates (PROTON in Malaysia, Renault Korea, Renault Brazil) and joint ventures (Horse Powertrain with Renault/Aramco).

business_model.summary: Geely earns the large majority of revenue from wholesale/retail sales of complete vehicles (ICE, PHEV, BEV, HEV) across its Geely/Geely Galaxy, LYNK & CO and ZEEKR brands, supplemented by auto parts/components sales, after-sales service, and income from financing/JV associates (e.g., Genius AFC auto-finance JV, Horse Powertrain engine/transmission JV). Revenue is overwhelmingly transactional (unit sales) rather than recurring, though vehicle financing, extended service contracts, subscription services (historically at LYNK & CO Europe, since discontinued) and software/driver-assistance features add smaller recurring-like streams. FY2025 revenue was restated upward across FY2021-FY2024 (e.g., FY2024 from RMB240.2bn to RMB275.9bn) after the Group adopted merger/pooling-of-interests accounting for common-control acquisitions of ZEEKR and LYNK & CO, consolidating entities previously held outside the listco by parent Geely Holding.

revenue_streams.name: Geely brand (Geely China Star ICE + Geely Galaxy NEV)
Parts, after-sales, financing JV income, other

business_model.customer_type: B2C retail/wholesale through dealer networks (first-tier dealer stores, direct and agency sales models), plus auto-finance partnerships; no meaningful direct enterprise/fleet disclosure segment
business_model.geographic_mix: China ~86% of 2025 wholesale volume (2,604,470 units), exports ~14% (420,097 units) across 86+ countries; overseas production in Egypt, Indonesia, Kazakhstan and via local partners/JVs in Malaysia, South Korea, Brazil

competitive_position.market_position: Second-largest Chinese passenger-vehicle group by domestic wholesale volume in 2025 (10.8% China market share, second only to BYD), and among the top Chinese groups globally (~4.6% global share in H1 2026, 7th largest automaker group). Fastest NEV brand in history to reach 1 million annual unit sales (Geely Galaxy, 29 months). Geely China Star has led indigenous-brand ICE passenger vehicle sales in China for nine consecutive years.

moat_factors.description: 14 domestic plants (2.6m annual capacity) plus 12 overseas plants, in-house battery/powertrain/driver-assistance R&D (InfiMotion, Qianli Intelligent Driving JV), and shared GEA/GEA Evo/SEA-S architectures spread R&D and component costs across Geely, Galaxy, LYNK & CO and ZEEKR

moat_factors.factor: Multi-brand portfolio covering mass-market to luxury
moat_factors.description: Geely/Galaxy (mass-market), LYNK & CO (mid-to-high-end), ZEEKR (luxury) allows price-segment coverage without brand cannibalization, though integration risk remains

"Full-Domain AI", G-ASD driver assistance system, Xingrui Intelligent Computing Centre, and the Qianli Intelligent Driving JV aim to keep pace with China's intelligence race, though Geely trails BYD/Huawei-ecosystem brands in brand recognition for ADAS

moat_factors.factor: Global distribution network and overseas manufacturing footprint
moat_factors.description: 76 sales agents/1,263 outlets (Geely brand) across 86 countries, plus associate relationships (PROTON, Renault Korea, Renault Brazil) provide a globalization channel that is harder for pure domestic challengers to replicate quickly

Access to Geely Holding's broader technology/supply chain (Volvo Cars, Polestar, Lotus engineering) via related-party and licensing arrangements, though this also creates related-party/connected-transaction complexity

BYD retains larger scale, deeper in-house battery (Blade/LFP) cost advantages and broader NEV-only brand recognition; Geely still carries a larger ICE legacy mix that dilutes average NEV economics versus pure-NEV peers

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on the intensely competitive, price-war-affected Chinese domestic market (~86% of volume)
Average selling price per vehicle declined (RMB103,000 in 2025 vs RMB112,000 in 2024) as NEV mass-market mix (Geely Galaxy) grows, pressuring blended margins

History of complex related-party transactions and corporate restructurings (ZEEKR privatisation, LYNK & CO acquisition, Horse Powertrain contribution, multiple common-control acquisitions) with multi-year financial restatements that complicate trend analysis

Minority/NCI-heavy structure historically at ZEEKR and LYNK & CO (now resolved via privatisation/full ownership) still leaves JV/associate stakes (Horse Powertrain, InfiMotion, PROTON, Renault Korea/Brazil) exposed to partner-specific execution risk
Export growth concentrated in emerging markets exposed to FX volatility (Russian ruble, other emerging-market currencies cited as risk factors)

growth_drivers: Continued "One Geely" brand integration (ZEEKR privatisation complete Dec-2025; LYNK & CO folded into ZEEKR/Geely in Feb-2025) eliminating redundant R&D/procurement spend and targeting cost synergies across brands
NEV mix shift: NEV sales volume up 90% YoY in 2025 to 1.69m units (56% of total), with 2026 group sales target of 3.45m units (+14% YoY)

GEA/GEA Evo/SEA-S platform-based new model cadence (Galaxy Xingyao 8, A7, M9, Xingyao 6; LYNK & CO 900/10 EM-P; ZEEKR 9X/007 GT) driving record volumes and premiumization (three flagship SUVs launched across all three brands in 2025)

Accelerating globalization: export volume +1% in 2025 to 420,097 units with NEV exports +240%; new overseas markets entered (UK, Italy, Poland, Australia, NZ, Vietnam, Indonesia, Brazil, South Africa); new plants in Egypt/Indonesia/Kazakhstan; Renault Brazil JV entry (21.29% stake) for Latin America access; continued PROTON (Malaysia) and Renault Korea technology-sharing
Full-domain AI/driver-assistance rollout (G-ASD system, World Action Model, Qianli Intelligent Driving JV) to support higher-ASP, higher-margin intelligent vehicle features
Horse Powertrain JV monetizing ICE/hybrid powertrain technology globally (RMB99.1bn revenue, RMB3.95bn net profit in 2025) while funding alternative-fuel R&D
HK$2.3 billion share buy-back program (initiated Oct/Dec 2025) signaling capital-return intent alongside growth investment

business.description: China's NEV/ICE price war has compressed industry-wide margins; Geely's average selling price fell ~8% YoY in 2025 even as volumes grew, and Beijing has repeatedly (2025-2026) summoned automakers over 'irrational competition' without stopping discounting

Consolidating ZEEKR, LYNK & CO, Geely Sunwoda disposals, InfiMotion and Qianli Intelligent Driving JV restructurings in rapid succession creates integration, governance and reporting complexity; multiple comparative-period restatements already required

business.risk: Competitive intensity from BYD and new entrants
business.description: BYD remains larger and more vertically integrated in batteries; Huawei-ecosystem brands (HIMA/Aito), Xiaomi, Leapmotor and others are aggressively gaining share in the same NEV price bands
Historical reliance on Geely Holding-affiliated dealership networks (Connected Automobile Dealers), only partly internalized via 2025 acquisitions

financial.description: Total borrowings rose 141% YoY to RMB18.3bn in 2025 (gearing ratio up to 19.8% from 8.8%) to fund the LYNK & CO acquisition and ZEEKR privatisation; current ratio slipped to 0.89x

Exposure to HKD, USD, EUR, SEK and RUB from export sales, overseas subsidiaries and emerging-market operations; 2025 results benefited from an FX gain (RMB2.43bn) that reversed a 2024 FX loss (RMB1.36bn), introducing earnings volatility unrelated to core operations

One-off items (gain on deemed disposal of Horse Powertrain stake in 2024, FX swings, impairments) create a wide gap between reported net income and management's 'core' profit metric, complicating year-over-year comparability

regulatory.risk: EU and other tariffs on Chinese-made EVs
regulatory.description: EU anti-subsidy tariffs applied to Chinese EV exporters (Geely assessed around 20% on top of the 10% base tariff in the original 2024 determination) directly affect export economics into Europe; trade-policy uncertainty (potential further US/EU/other-market tariff actions) is an ongoing overhang on the globalization strategy

MIIT/SAMR have repeatedly summoned automakers (most recently June 2026) over suspected irrational competition and introduced below-cost-sale and 60-day supplier-payment rules; compliance costs and uncertain enforcement effectiveness persist

Numerous common-control transactions with Geely Holding and its affiliates (dealer networks, Sunwoda disposal, LYNK & CO/ZEEKR transfers) require ongoing HKEX connected-transaction compliance and are accounted for via merger accounting that affects comparability
Reduction of China's NEV tax incentives/trade-in subsidies slated for 2026 could dampen near-term demand (UBS expects China passenger-car sales to fall modestly in 2026)

macro.description: Passenger vehicle demand sensitive to broader Chinese consumer confidence, property-sector weakness and GDP growth trends
US-China and EU-China trade tensions, supply-chain restructuring and potential further tariff escalation directly threaten the export-led growth strategy that is central to Geely's 2026+ plan

Battery raw materials (lithium, nickel, cobalt), semiconductors and other NEV components are exposed to global price cycles; management specifically flagged upward cost pressure from cross-industry competition for electronic components in its 2026 outlook

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China NEV penetration exceeded 50% of the domestic passenger vehicle market in 2025 (54.0% including BEV+PHEV) and is entering a 'mature' phase; industry growth is shifting from electrification to vehicle intelligence (ADAS/AI) and globalization as the next competitive battlegrounds. China's total passenger vehicle wholesale volume (incl. exports) grew 9.2% YoY in 2025 to 30.1 million units; 2026 growth is expected to moderate as subsidies phase down.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical — auto demand tracks consumer confidence and disposable income, though Chinese government stimulus (trade-in programs, NEV tax breaks) has smoothed some cyclicality; capital-intensive manufacturing model creates operating leverage in downturns
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — auto-finance JV (Genius AFC) profitability is sensitive to interest rates (2025 net profit down 41% YoY partly from declining rates/competition); higher borrowings (RMB18.3bn, up from RMB7.6bn) increase direct interest-rate exposure on the balance sheet
key_input_costs: Electronic components (broadly, amid cross-industry competition for supply)

recent_developments.event: Completed privatisation of ZEEKR, acquiring all outstanding ZEEKR shares/ADSs (cash or Geely ADS consideration shares); ZEEKR delisted from NYSE and became a wholly-owned subsidiary
Commenced HK$2.3 billion automatic share buy-back program via Morgan Stanley; ~22.4 million shares repurchased for ~HK$384.7 million by year-end 2025, cancelled Feb-2026
Board approved and finalized terms of the HK$2.3bn buy-back program
Signed merger agreement for ZEEKR privatisation (US$2.687 cash or 1.23 Geely consideration shares per ZEEKR share)

Completed ZEEKR's acquisition of LYNK & CO (49% Ningbo Geely / 51% Zhejiang ZEEKR), consolidating LYNK & CO into Group accounts; total consideration/payments of ~RMB9.1bn plus RMB367m capital subscription

Change in accounting policy for common-control business combinations (acquisition method to pooling-of-interests/merger accounting), applied retrospectively, driving the restatement of FY2021-FY2024 financials (FY2024 revenue restated from RMB240.2bn to RMB275.9bn)

FY2025 revenue RMB345.2bn (+25% YoY), record sales volume of 3,024,567 units (+39% YoY, exceeding the raised 3m-unit target); profit attributable to owners RMB16.85bn (+0.2% YoY, flattered by prior-year one-off Horse Powertrain gain); final dividend raised to HK$0.50/share from HK$0.33

H1 2026 results: record H1 revenue RMB173.6bn (+16% YoY, sixth consecutive year of H1 growth); gross margin expanded to 17.9%; core profit (management-adjusted) +46% YoY to ~RMB9.68bn even as reported net profit fell ~2% YoY to RMB9.09bn; exports +157.6% YoY to 474,228 units offsetting a 22.6% domestic volume decline

Geely overtook BYD in several early-2026 monthly domestic sales rankings (e.g., January and combined Jan-Feb 2026) as BYD sales fell amid tax-break rollback and intensified competition; September 2026 was Geely's highest monthly sales total of the year (292,168 units, +6.97% YoY)
Chinese regulators (MIIT/SAMR) continued summoning automakers over 'irrational' price competition, most recently around June 2026, with limited effect on actual discounting behavior
EU anti-subsidy tariffs on Chinese-made EVs (Geely assessed near 20% on top of a 10% base tariff) remain a live constraint on European export economics, with periodic EU-China negotiation rounds

guidance.as_of: FY2025 Annual Report (March 2026) and H1 2026 results (August 2026)

items.notes: Represents ~14% YoY increase over the 3,024,567 units achieved in FY2025, which itself exceeded a mid-year-raised target of 3 million units

items.target: approximately RMB16 billion (excluding acquisitions via business combinations)
items.notes: FY2025 actual capex was RMB17.9bn, above the RMB15bn FY2025 budget, reflecting higher R&D/electrification investment; FY2026 budget set at RMB16bn for new model R&D, intelligent technology and production-facility upgrades

items.target: Advance 'full-domain AI strategy' to Phase 2.0; scale G-ASD driver-assistance system toward L3/L4 evolution
items.notes: Qualitative strategic target rather than a quantified KPI; follows completion of the 'Smart Geely 2025' strategy

items.target: Continue increasing NEV share of total sales volume beyond the 56% achieved in FY2025
items.notes: No explicit numeric FY2026 NEV-mix target disclosed in the annual report; direction of travel reaffirmed in Chairman's Statement and Outlook section

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Li Shu Fu's FY2025 letter emphasized 'critical junctures' framing for 2026 (Geely's 40th anniversary), citing geopolitical fluctuation, supply-chain restructuring and climate transition as structural challenges, alongside a 'brutal phase' of cost/technology/scale competition in electrification and an intelligence race shifting from 'functional' to 'scenario-based' intelligence. Management highlighted the completed 'One Geely' brand integration (Geely, LYNK & CO, ZEEKR) as the basis for cost synergies and competitiveness, and reiterated a 'platforms + ecosystems' framing for future competition (vehicle-to-cloud, mobility data, low-orbit satellite communications). H1 2026 commentary (per press coverage) emphasized that export strength (+157.6% YoY) is offsetting domestic-volume softness (-22.6% YoY) tied to the ongoing China price war and subsidy normalization.

bull_case: Record FY2025 and H1 2026 results with accelerating NEV mix (56% of volume) and margin expansion (gross margin up to 17.9% in H1 2026) show the brand-integration/scale strategy is working despite a brutal domestic pricing environment

Export volumes are growing explosively (+157.6% YoY in H1 2026, +240% for NEV exports in FY2025) and diversifying into Latin America (Renault Brazil), Southeast Asia, Africa and Australia, reducing reliance on the saturated, price-war-afflicted Chinese market

Completed 'One Geely' consolidation (ZEEKR privatisation, LYNK & CO integration) simplifies the corporate structure, eliminates related-party overlap/compliance burden, and should unlock cross-brand R&D, supply-chain and procurement synergies going forward

Strong analyst sentiment (consensus 'Strong Buy', price targets broadly HK$27-30 from CICC, Citi, JPMorgan, Huachuang, CLSA as of mid-2026) and an active HK$2.3bn buyback signal confidence from both the sell-side and management
Geely has overtaken BYD in several 2026 monthly domestic sales rankings, suggesting genuine share gains against China's largest NEV maker rather than merely riding the broader market
bear_case: China's EV/ICE price war remains unresolved despite repeated regulatory intervention (MIIT/SAMR summons through 2026); average selling price per vehicle has already declined and further discounting could erode the margin gains achieved in FY2025/H1 2026

Domestic volumes fell 22.6% YoY in H1 2026 even as total volume grew only modestly, indicating the core China market is weakening and growth is increasingly dependent on exports, which carry their own tariff and FX risks

EU and potential other-market tariffs on Chinese-made EVs (Geely assessed near 20% in the original EU determination) directly tax the export growth engine that bulls are relying on, and trade-policy risk could escalate further

Financial comparability is complicated by repeated restatements (FY2021-FY2024 revenue revised up via merger accounting for ZEEKR/LYNK & CO) and a widening gap between 'core' and reported profit, making it harder for investors to assess underlying earnings quality

Rising leverage (borrowings up 141% YoY to RMB18.3bn, gearing up to 19.8%, current ratio below 1.0x) to fund the LYNK & CO and ZEEKR privatisation deals reduces balance-sheet flexibility just as competitive and regulatory pressures intensify
